mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which typically boosts corporate revenues and profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in periods of rising RSAFS, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.0% signals a tight labor market, which typically increases wage pressures and corporate profitability, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls below 5.0%, 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust economic activity across manufacturing and construction sectors, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When both INDPRO and HOUST rise, 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, an increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs, which typically depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In monetary tightening cycles, 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising CPI (CPIAUCSL) indicates increasing inflation, which typically erodes real corporate profits and prompts central bank tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL rises, 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 indicates economic contraction, which typically reduces corporate output and profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls below 100.0, 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in employment (PAYEMS) and fall in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which typically boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls, 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During housing market expansions, rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong demand for residential construction, which typically boosts related industries and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In housing market expansions, 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
